title: Phase 3: Audit log tamper-proof application
description:
## Goal
Apply the existing hash-chain JSONL writer/verify (in `toppy-core::audit`) to actual audit log emission and verification flows.

## Implementation
- Identify where audit logs are currently written (CLI + GW).
- Wire in chained writer so each event links to previous hash.
- Add `toppy audit verify` (or equivalent) to validate the local log.
- Decide on keying/seed strategy (local-only first; remote later).

## Acceptance
- A modified/edited JSONL entry is detected by verify.
- Unit tests cover writer + verifier integration.
notes: Wired audit hash-chain into CLI flows (doctor/up) and added  (uses TOPPY_AUDIT_LOG / config.audit_log_path / default path). Added helper append_event + tests and ensured audit writer creates parent dirs.

title: Phase 3: CONNECT-UDP (MASQUE) spike
description:
## Goal
Add a path toward CONNECT-UDP support so UDP apps can traverse the tunnel.

## Scope (spike)
- Confirm what subset we want first: Extended CONNECT with `:protocol=connect-udp` and HTTP Datagrams.
- Prototype protocol encode/decode in `toppy-proto` (varint context id + payload) if not already present.
- Gateway: accept CONNECT-UDP and provide a simple datagram echo.
- CLI doctor: add checks like `masque.connect_udp` and `masque.connect_udp.datagram`.

## Acceptance
- Doctor can report pass/fail for CONNECT-UDP handshake and datagram echo.
- Integration test runs in CI (compose + doctor).
notes: Integration gate now asserts doctor CONNECT-UDP checks pass (masque.connect_udp + masque.connect_udp.datagram). GW already accepts CONNECT-UDP and echoes HTTP Datagrams; core doctor already implements handshake+echo checks.

title: S5: Windows RDP E2E reachability check
description:
## Context
Add Windows runner E2E coverage for RDP port (3389) similar to existing Linux TCP reachability checks. This is currently documented as a TODO in `TODO.md` (S5).

## Implementation
- Ensure CI job can be triggered via `workflow_dispatch` with input `rdp_host`.
- Use `scripts/e2e-rdp.ps1` with `TOPPY_E2E_RDP_HOST` (or workflow input) to run:
  - allow: start `toppy up --target <rdp_host>:3389` and verify local listener accepts TCP
  - deny: `toppy up --target <rdp_host>:3390` fails with policy deny and no listener
- Capture logs/artifacts so failures are diagnosable.

## Acceptance
- allow path succeeds (TCP connect to local forwarded port)
- deny path fails with policy deny and local port is not open
- doctor reports `policy.denied` as `fail` and includes reason in summary
notes: Implemented Windows RDP E2E: resolves hostname->IPv4, verifies allowed --once exit, checks policy.denied summary includes reason, uploads artifacts from CI.
